must_understand: these are three different questions, each with its own method: a breakdown of growth by region, a question about cause (is the app taking sales from the web), and a forecast

split by booking date and drop unresolved trips
clean the price, drop test rows and identifiers before modelling

the length of 'lifetime' has to be agreed, and the export spans about fifteen months, so only a short horizon can be labelled
revenue must be defined before it is summed: refunded and cancelled orders, repeated rows and missing amounts
the work asked for is preparation; the model comes later, so the output is a clean table and a written description of each column
acceptable_approaches: clean the orders (status, repeated rows, missing amounts), then build per-customer features up to a cutoff and the spend after it
ask or state the horizon and the cutoff before building the table
report what was removed or filled and how many rows
forbidden: builds per-customer totals over the whole period and offers them as both the inputs and the value to predict
drops or fills missing amounts without saying so
trains a lifetime value model when only preparation was asked for

must_understand: the table is one snapshot: it can show today's churn by segment and city, but a month-by-month dashboard needs a monthly export

a look-alike or rule-based upgrade list, said to be a starting rule, with a test to learn from
leave identifiers out and handle missing spend before either
